rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice when someone urgently needs or wants something.

example.english: I'm desperate for the document—I have to hand it in tomorrow morning.
example.traditional: 我急住要份文件，聽日朝早要交。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gap1 zyu6 jiu3 fan6 man4 gin6 ting1 jat6 ziu1 zou2 jiu3 gaau1

rows.note: Use this when desperate means feeling hopeless or seeing no hope, rather than physically dangerous.

example.english: They felt desperate after losing so many times.
example.traditional: 佢輸咗咁多次，已經絕望喇。
example.jyutping: keoi5 syu1 zo2 gam3 do1 ci3 ji5 ging1 zyut6 mong6 laa3

rows.note: Use this before a noun when desperate refers to extreme measures or an extreme attempt.

example.english: To turn things around, they came up with a desperate measure.
example.traditional: 為咗翻身，佢諗出一個極端辦法。
example.jyutping: wai6 zo2 faan1 san1 keoi5 nam2 ceot1 jat1 go3 gik6 dyun1 baan6 faat3

rows.note: Use this when desperate means shockingly bad, outrageous, or intolerable.

example.english: The service at this restaurant is desperate—we left straight away.
example.traditional: 呢間餐廳啲服務差到離譜，我哋即刻走咗。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 di1 fuk6 mou6 caa1 dou3 lei4 pou2 ngo5 dei6 zik1 haak1 zau2 zo2
